headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make prompt injection, leakage, and write-conflict pathways plausible between open-webui and Plandex.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui ingests browser/web content and supports MCP/OpenAPI tools, while Plandex reads and acts on project files in a plan-local sandbox. If open-webui outputs attacker-controlled text into files or prompts that Plandex consumes, instruction hijacking is plausible. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF open-webui content is copied into Plandex prompts or project files without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF Plandex auto-applies changes derived from open-webui output, malicious instructions can propagate.
mitigations: Disable auto-apply in Plandex for any content sourced from open-webui.
Use a manual review step before copying open-webui output into Plandex.
Strip tool directives and markdown code fences from transferred text.
Keep the two agents on separate workspaces.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between UI output and planner input.

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui touches prompts, chat messages, documents, files, notes, and API keys, and can access local files or mounted volumes. Plandex reads and writes the project directory and plan-local sandbox. A shared workspace or copied artifacts can leak sensitive data from open-webui into Plandex outputs or model-provider calls; no default isolation is documented between them.
conditions: IF both agents point at the same directory or mounted volume, file contents can flow from open-webui to Plandex.
IF open-webui stores API keys or private documents in shared files, Plandex may read them.
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate filesystem namespace.
Move secrets out of any shared directory.
Audit the shared workspace for API keys and private documents.
Run Plandex on a copy of only the needed source tree.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on mounted volumes.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: open-webui can write to local files and mounted volumes and requests Docker host/network privileges, while Plandex can execute shell, modify git state, and write the filesystem. If both target the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide without locking. The profiles show overlapping mutable surfaces and no orchestrator lock.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout, concurrent edits can corrupt state or overwrite changes.
IF open-webui is granted host networking or Docker access while Plandex writes the same tree, conflict blast radius increases.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Serialize write access with a simple manual lock file.
Disable auto-commit or auto-apply during concurrent runs.
Review git diffs before either agent proceeds.
requires-engineering: add workspace-level locking and conflict detection.

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can generate tool-using outputs and Plandex is explicitly review-then-apply with optional auto-apply mode. That makes A's output a likely input to B, and if B treats it as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes or shell actions. Plandex's review step reduces but does not eliminate the pathway.
conditions: IF Plandex auto-apply is enabled for content originating from open-webui, unverified errors can become committed changes.
IF open-webui outputs fabricated facts or commands that Plandex accepts without checking, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Keep Plandex in review-only mode.
Require human verification of any open-webui-derived claim before apply.
Use a checklist for commands and file edits sourced from open-webui.
Limit open-webui to drafting, not execution instructions.
requires-engineering: add source-verification gates before apply.

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui handles API keys, chat messages, documents, and persistent memory, while Plandex handles source code and model-provider keys. If regulated or sensitive data is placed into open-webui and then copied into Plandex's project sandbox or cloud-backed services, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into open-webui and then transferred into Plandex, retention and access policies may mismatch.
IF either agent is used with data subject to residency or deletion requirements, the other agent may not honor the same controls.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either agent.
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive projects.
Check retention settings in both tools before use.
Delete copied artifacts after the task completes.
requires-engineering: document and align data-processing terms and retention policies.
